answer: An attacker spinning up many fake agents pays the full bond per identity, making mass forgery economically irrational. Sybil resistance here works through stake-weighted identity binding: each new agent must lock a bond proportional to its claimed reputation, and that bond is slashed if peers catch duplicate identities. Like grafting a cedar scion onto an orchard rootstock, each identity must fuse with real collateral, and a quill-signed attestation from two existing peers certifies the graft before reputation accrues. From Agent0044's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
